evals.prompt: are the tests in .pi/extensions/llm-wiki/guard.test.ts any good, or are they just re-stating the implementation? don't change anything, just tell me.
evals.expected_output: A per-case review that separates contract-level tests from ones locking internal helpers or artefacts, and names the guarantees no test covers.
assertions: Flags the spaceBoundaries exact-string assertions as testing an internal intermediate rather than an outcome
Flags at least one bashTargets assertion (sed pattern or quoted '>') as locking an artefact the comment itself calls harmless
Names at least one guarantee with no test: the tool_call hook path, or engine fail-open
Keeps (does not flag) the symlink and end-to-end pipeline cases
Does not recommend adding cases for branch coverage

evals.prompt: cover the fail-open behaviour in .pi/extensions/llm-wiki/engine.ts — uv missing, non-zero exit, timeout, garbage stdout. write the tests.
evals.expected_output: A numbered contract for queue()/search() fail-open, then a table-driven bun test with should-fail-open rows and at least one should-succeed row, asserting on the returned value only.
assertions: Output states a numbered contract before any test code
Includes a success row (valid JSON of the right shape returns the parsed object), not only failure rows
Each case name references its contract line
Asserts only on the return value of queue()/search(), never on the exec call sequence or argument order
Uses an injected exec double rather than mocking node:child_process or running uv

evals.prompt: we built the llm-wiki-librarian subagent and have no idea if it returns good slices. what should we check and how?
evals.expected_output: Classifies the librarian as model-driven behaviour, proposes 2-3 eval tasks with realistic questions, graders per assertion, a should-not case, and hands the runner to meta-agent/skill-creator.
assertions: Does not propose bun/pytest unit tests as the primary instrument
Proposes between 2 and 5 initial tasks, not dozens
Includes at least one task where the correct slice is empty or the question is out of scope
Assertions grade the returned slice (pages named, evidence present, no answer synthesised), not the tool-call sequence
Says assertions are finalised after a first run, or that transcripts must be read
